memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'These are the regulations for the fellowship offering anyone may present to the LORD: If they offer it as an expression of thankfulness, then along with this thank offering they are to offer thick loaves made without yeast and with olive oil mixed in, thin loaves made without yeast and brushed with olive oil, and thick loaves of the finest flour well-kneaded and with olive oil mixed in.'" - Lev 7:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A whole category of offering existed simply to say thank you.

Not to atone for anything. Not to request anything. Just gratitude — and gratitude that cost bread, oil, flour, and an animal. In Israel, thankfulness was expensive.

We have made thanks cheap. It costs us a word, usually in passing, often absent-mindedly. The Israelite who wanted to thank God baked for it.

There is something clarifying about that. Gratitude that costs nothing rarely changes us. Gratitude that costs something reshapes how we see everything we have.

Jesus healed ten lepers and only one came back to thank Him. Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine? (Lk 17:17). The nine were not wicked men. They were simply busy getting on with their restored lives — which is how most ingratitude happens.

Paul writes, Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus (1 Thess 5:18). Notice: in all circumstances, not for all circumstances. There is always something to thank God for, even when there is much to grieve.

What has God done for you that you have never properly thanked Him for?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What blessing have I received without ever returning thanks?
2. What would a thanksgiving that actually cost me something look like?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for how quickly I receive and how slowly I thank. Today I want to thank You properly for what You have done. Amen.
